Name: Debbie Ross
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

My students are eager to please and learn. This process provided new insights into the way students conduct research for a writing task. I really enjoyed the whole aspect of the layering process and plan to continue this as a way to teache students how to conduct research for future projects. Sometimes it is easy to forget how frustrating a writing task can be when you do really know were to begin. This process is a great way for students to conduct research without becoming frustrated by the process.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
I had a couple of students share some of the insights they gained by reading different pieces and trying to understand the differences in the thought process of the persons writing the articles. My juniors are anxious to please and are avid learners, but sometimes having a variety of ways to complete the same tasks is very beneficial to the different types of learners.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
The amount of work they put into this project and the amount of learning that took place is visible in the work that was handed in for a grade. I had a several students voice comments stating they were really surprised at how much they learned about a topic they knew nothing about prior to the activity.
